title: Chapter 1091
paragraphs: Chapter 1091
Episode 255. The Death of Kelliark Zipple, and....(8)
Lokia's negotiation had failed.
Lucy, who had refused the proposal, immediately began to attack Lokia's clone. In the end, she couldn't even capture the clone.
That night, Murakan found Lucy standing alone in the hanging garden of Tikan Palace.
“Lucy.”
“Murakan.”
Murakan gave a bitter smile as he opened the bottle of liquor he had brought.
“Damn... I don't know what to say. I'm terrible at comforting, you know. It's strange to ask if you're okay, too. I'm sorry.”
“What is there for Murakan to be sorry about. I'm not the only one who has lost a child in this horrific world.”
The two of them looked up at the dark night sky and drank their cups.
“...Lokia can't kill Hailyn anyway. She'll judge that her use value hasn't completely disappeared even though she failed in this negotiation.”
“Huuu.”
“And even if she does die... if her power from Araxion is separated, and she can just die as an ordinary human. That too would be a liberation for that child.”
“The era is cruel. A thousand years ago, and now.”
“It is. Then and now, it's an era where you can't protect anything if you're not strong.”
For a while, the sound of them drinking in silence continued.
“...Has the Young Patriarch made a decision?”
“Yes... he said he's going to the Black Sea.”
“It must be because he is certain that Temar's left arm is related to Solderet's arrangement there.”
Murakan nodded his head.

“It feels like a good judgment. We can't win if we're just being dragged around by the enemies while protecting our home base. It's a fact that was already proven a thousand years ago, especially against the Zipple.”
The Black Sea.
Jin had made the judgment that the coalition had to rendezvous with Chiron's expedition for now. They could no longer just sit and wait for them to return.

Of course, due to the nature of the region known as the Black Sea, they wouldn't be able to succeed in rendezvousing in just a day or two. However, the coalition now possessed military strength and special abilities that were incomparable to when Chiron first left for the Black Sea. Even the Sun God Cult had once created a dimensional gate that encompassed the Black Sea.

“The burden that the Young Patriarch carries is incomparable to mine, who has just one daughter held hostage. He has to make judgments while carrying the weight of all life except for the enemy at every moment.”
Lucy turned around as she emptied her last cup.
“Let's go, Murakan. We are Runcandels. If we were to collapse from pain and sorrow while fighting, we would have been ruined a thousand years ago.”
A day passed.
There were still no particular clues about the whereabouts of Kelliark and Malugia. And the coalition members were preparing to leave for the Black Sea.
All the Genesis Knights were heading for the Black Sea.

The coalition had no intention of sending just some of their main forces for this Black Sea trip. All the Genesis Knights, the flagship Sarah, the Plutonian Golden Fleet, and the Battle God Temple main hall's flying fortress, 'Lafrarosa.'
They had formed a force that could break through the Black Sea in the shortest possible time to find Chiron.
There was no turning back. After all, if they didn't rendezvous with Chiron and obtain Solderet's arrangement, there was no future.
“It is thanks to Lord Focal and Lady Silkia. If it weren't for you two, we wouldn't have been able to move this quickly.”
Jin said as he looked at the two. Focal and Silkia were playing a decisive role in this trip to the Black Sea.
Beltian, the ego of Destruction, had received no benefit from Malugia in this battle. Rather, he was bound by Focal's authority and had become the power source for the flying fortress Lafrarosa.

Silkia was scheduled to form a dimensional gate that led directly to the depths of the Black Sea, along with Focal. Depending on the situation after their arrival, it might even be possible to create a dimensional gate that connected to a point beyond the depths.
“Father must be aware that something has happened in the mortal world. Even if not in great detail, he must surely know that great enemies that even he cannot handle alone have awoken.”
Jin nodded at Luna's words.

“Father must also feel like he's been struck by a bolt from the blue. Don't you think there was a part of him that believed his destiny would be fulfilled by subjugating the five kings of the Black Sea?”

“That's right. During the expedition, before he overcame his demonic transformation, Father... looked as if he was planning to die along with the five kings of the Black Sea. I know it's a bit much to feel this way while people are dying all over the world, but it's true that I'm a little excited.”
Chiron Runcandel.

In Runcandel, that name was still the family's last bastion and a symbol of invincibility. Now that Kelliark and Malugia had appeared, he could no longer be said to be truly invincible, but the influence that one man held was still as valid as ever.
“It will be reassuring. When he returns. But he won't return just by us meeting him and explaining the situation in detail. As Brother Jin said, he already has his destiny.”
The last remaining king of the Black Sea, Morganiel. Vahn was certain that Chiron would not return unless he killed him.
“However, he won't refuse our help in his destiny.”
“That's right, Lord Vahn. Because Father has changed.”
Go to the Black Sea, find Chiron, subjugate Morganiel together, and then return to the mortal world.

That was the best outcome the coalition could hope for from this endeavor. Although Morganiel was surely the strongest of the five kings of the Black Sea, the coalition did not think he was on a level comparable to Kelliark or Malugia.
“As all the Genesis Knights are gathering, we will surely capture Morganiel with minimal damage and find Solderet's final arrangement.”
“Brother Jin, when will we depart?”
“If there are no decisive peculiarities in Valeria's report at midnight, we will depart immediately.”
“Understood.”
Outside the conference room, all the coalition members were moving about busily.
Just because they were throwing the gamble of rendezvousing with Chiron did not mean they were completely abandoning the mortal world during that period.
Migration.

The Vamel Alliance was beginning the work of migrating the ordinary people of the mortal world to the Underworld. Although there was no longer any fundamentally safe place in the world, the underground was still better than the surface.

During the fierce battle between Malugia and Kelliark that destroyed the Empire, the Underworld had received no damage. Of course, since the underground was currently under reconstruction, the standard of living was bound to drop sharply compared to the mortal world, but the majority of people applied for migration, even if it meant enduring that.

There were not a few who refused the migration, saying they would rather die in their homeland. The coalition members respected all of those opinions. Not to reduce their workload, but because everyone had the right to choose their life. Especially in a situation like this.
Jin meditated as he waited for midnight.
The countless number of possibilities that would arise in the wars to come were floating roughly in his mind. At every moment, he had to grasp the most brilliant move among them.
As midnight approached, Orgal came to find Jin before Valeria.
[Jin.]
“Orgal, did the Witch give an answer?”

[Damn it, no. I relayed your words through the three demons, but it seems no one can meet the Witch right now. Not just me, but even them, the residents of the Abyss. It seems she was affected by the battle between Malugia and Kelliark.]
“Understood.”
[I'll let you know again if I hear any news. You'll be heading to the Black Sea soon, right?]
“Yes. Since our most important forces will be absent for a while, you'll have a lot to do.”

[Don't worry. Even if those bastards suddenly strike us, we'll survive somehow until you return. We've been known for our running away since way back, haven't we? It was always like that in other dimensions too. My main pattern was to run to somehow seize an opportunity, then get cornered, fight like hell, and die a glorious death. Compared to that, now, there is still hope.]
Orgal grinned and held out his fist to Jin. For the first time, Jin lightly bumped his fist against his and smiled.
“I'll be back as soon as possible.”
[Yeah, travel safely.]
The moment Orgal left, the hallway of the conference room became noisy. Valeria had returned.
“Jin.”
“You've worked hard, Valeria. Did the records on Malugia and Kelliark come out?”
“Not yet for Malugia, but I found one record on Kelliark. It's just as Veradin said. He is conscious of Octavia Zipple.”
1st Passage, Demon ArmyHeadquarters.

Due to Malugia's attack, the headquarters was in a messy state, unlike before. Most of the dimensional gates that led to each world were crushed and emitting a horrific energy, and Kelliark Zipple was sitting in a ruined medical room with transparent tubes stuck all over his body.
“Octavia.”
At Kelliark's cracked voice, Octavia raised her head.

When she had first come here, she had been in a state of much more serious injury than Kelliark. Kelliark had used the treatment device on Octavia first, and she had become as clean as if she had received the blood of Numerus.
“Now you will be able to believe all the stories I have told you. The multiple worlds, the endlessly connected war of all dimensions, etc.”
“In that case, in this world, survive.”
“Pardon?”

“While eliminating and conquering numerous dimensions. Sometimes, things that never change catch my eye. Strangely enough. One of them is you, Octavia. In all the worlds I have known, you have never once survived.”
